dct_description_sm: We sampled beaver abundance in the Watersheds of the Poplar and the Old Factory Rivers for three main reasons. As part of a larger project to understand the determinants of beaver abundance across the province of Quebec, the sampling of beaver abundance in the Wemindji region allowed us to narrow the limiting factors influencing beaver abundance in a transitional region (from dense populations in the south to the rare colonies of the tundra). At a regional level,  a spatially-explicit model was used to better understand the influence of forest fires on beaver ecology through correlative analysis of riparian vegetation and the location of beaver colonies. Finally, this work was part of a SSHERC CURA (Community University Research Alliance) project aiming at the creation of a culturally appropriate protected area encompassing both watersheds. Aerial pictures were taken to relate culturally important landscape features to Cree narratives. These pictures will be used in an interactive GIS program that will be made available to the Wemindji community.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK)
dct_title_s: Aerial surveys of beaver abundance in the Old Factory and Poplar watersheds, James Bay, Quebec
